question.prompt: Let \(\triangle ABC\) be an isosceles triangle with \(BC = AC\) and \(\angle ACB = 40^{\circ}.\) Construct the circle with diameter \(\overline{BC},\) and let \(D\) and \(E\) be the other intersection points of the circle with the sides \(\overline{AC}\) and \(\overline{AB},\) respectively. Let \(F\) be the intersection of the diagonals of the quadrilateral \(BCDE.\) What is the degree measure of \(\angle BFC ?\)

solutions.title: Use the diameter's right angles
solutions.explanation:
The diameter \(BC\) gives two right angles, which we can use in quadrilateral \(AEFD\).

Since \(AC=BC\), the angles at \(A\) and \(B\) are equal. Hence
\[
\angle BAC=\angle ABC=\frac{180^\circ-40^\circ}{2}=70^\circ.
\]
Because \(D\) and \(E\) lie on the circle with diameter \(BC\),
\[
\angle BDC=\angle BEC=90^\circ.
\]
Thus \(BD\perp AC\) and \(CE\perp AB\). The diagonals of \(BCDE\) are \(BD\) and \(CE\), so \(F\) lies on both. Consequently, \(\angle ADF=\angle AEF=90^\circ\).

The angle at \(A\) in quadrilateral \(AEFD\) is \(\angle DAE=70^\circ\). Using the quadrilateral's angle sum gives
\[
\angle DFE=360^\circ-90^\circ-90^\circ-70^\circ=110^\circ.
\]
Finally, \(\angle BFC\) and \(\angle DFE\) are vertical angles formed by \(BD\) and \(CE\), so they are equal. Therefore \(\boxed{\angle BFC=110^\circ}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
